lines: Two hard clippers with a display, each holding a polyphonic signal within a set voltage; leave the outputs unpatched and it works as a clip and logic monitor
The first signal to be clipped, polyphonic; its channels show on the display in blue, turning red while a channel is clipping
The first signal after clipping, held within plus or minus the clipping voltage
The second signal to be clipped, polyphonic
The second signal after clipping, held within plus or minus the clipping voltage
Sets the clipping voltage for both signals and every channel, 0-10V, starting at 5V; it does nothing while the Vclip input is patched
Sets the clipping voltage directly, one channel per clipping voltage over 0-20V, and takes over from the Vclip knob; a negative voltage counts as its positive value
Menu — Logic Monitoring — treats low-to-high and high-to-low changes alike on the display, which suits watching 0-10V logic with the clipping voltage at 5V; it does not work with bipolar signals
Three windowed comparators sharing one input, each putting out a gate while the input lies between its own two thresholds
The voltage all three comparators test, polyphonic; the channels patched here set how many channels each gate output carries
Sets the upper threshold for that comparator, -10V to +10V; the input must be under it for that gate to open
Sets the lower threshold for that comparator, -10V to +10V; the input must reach it for that gate to open
Goes to 10V while the input is inside that comparator's thresholds and 0V the rest of the time, one channel per input channel
Cycles that comparator through three modes: windowing with no light, lower threshold only with a red light, and upper threshold only with a blue light
Note — setting a comparator's upper threshold below its lower one splits the range in two, the lower threshold then passing everything above it and the upper threshold everything below it
Menu — Close interval toward zero — puts the equality test on the side nearer zero when a threshold is negative, changing which end of the window takes in its own voltage
Three separate sine oscillators running at low frequency, each with its own frequency control and modulation input
Sets that oscillator's frequency, 0.0039Hz to 1024Hz, starting at 2Hz
A bipolar sine wave, plus or minus 5V
A steady voltage here shifts that oscillator's frequency by an octave per volt, and a changing one modulates it; the channels patched here set that output's polyphony
An attenuverter for that oscillator's modulation input, -100% to +100%, starting at zero
Four sine oscillators running at low frequency from one shared frequency, each at its own ratio of it
Sets the frequency all four oscillators are worked out from, 0.015625Hz to 256Hz, starting at 2Hz
A steady voltage here shifts the shared frequency by an octave per volt, and a changing one modulates all four outputs; the channels patched here set the outputs' polyphony
Multiplies the frequency CV by -1, turning that input into an inverting one
Multiplies the shared frequency for that oscillator, 0.0039 times to 256 times, starting at unity; a red lamp comes on as the setting nears the 1/1024Hz to 1024Hz limits
A bipolar sine wave, plus or minus 5V
Note — with Negative CV mode on, 10V at the frequency CV input holds the output voltages where they are
Note — the red lamps beside the ratio knobs go out while the frequency CV input is patched, so they warn of nothing then
Menu — Extended Hold Range — multiplies the frequency CV by five, so 10V is enough to stop the oscillators completely
Menu — Preset — lists five factory ratio presets, named Golden 1.618, Silver 2.414, Bronze 3.303, Copper 4.236 and Nickel 5.193; each divides every output again by that ratio, from unity at the first
AND, OR and XOR gates of two inputs each and a NOT gate, all polyphonic, over 0-10V logic where anything above 1V counts as high
One of the two signals that gate combines; patch this one alone and the gate is applied across all the channels of this input instead, giving a single-channel result
The other of the two signals that gate combines; patch this one alone and its channels are inverted to the output
The result of that gate, 10V for high and 0V for low; with neither input patched it stays at 0V
The signal the NOT gate inverts, channel by channel
Each channel of the NOT input inverted; with nothing patched to that input it stays at 10V
Chooses how XOR combines the channels of a single input: off counts odd parity, on gives high only when exactly one channel is high
Note — a monophonic input is combined with every channel of a polyphonic one; two polyphonic inputs are matched channel for channel, and the unmatched channels are dropped
Gathers eight separate signals into one polyphonic cable of eight channels
Becomes the polyphonic channel of that number at the output
Carries all eight inputs as one eight-channel polyphonic signal
Note — an input left empty below a patched one takes a channel of the output all the same, and that channel carries 0V
Menu — Channels Merge — sets how many channels the output carries: Automatic, the default, gives as many channels as the highest-numbered patched input, or choose a fixed count from 1 to 8
Gathers four separate signals into one polyphonic cable, and splits a polyphonic cable back into four separate signals, in two sections that are not connected to each other
Becomes the polyphonic channel of that number at the merge output
Carries the four merge inputs as one four-channel polyphonic signal
The polyphonic signal whose channels are sent out separately
Carries the channel of that number from the split input, on its own
Note — merging a signal, quantizing it and splitting it again adds three sample delays to the pitch path; the SampleDelays modules can put the same delay on a gate path
Note — a merge input left empty below a patched one takes a channel of the merge output all the same, and that channel carries 0V

Menu — Channels Merge — sets how many channels the merge output carries: Automatic, the default, gives as many channels as the highest-numbered patched merge input, or choose a fixed count from 1 to 4
Four chords of four notes each, set by knob in any temperament from 1 to 34 notes per octave, one chord at a time sent out on a polyphonic cable
Sets that note of that chord within the octave, from 0 up to one less than the notes-per-octave setting
Sets the octave of that note of that chord, -4 to +4
Sets the temperament, 1 to 34 notes in the octave, starting at 12
Chooses the chord that reaches the output: 0V for A, 1V for B, 2V for C, 3V for D, with a blue lamp on the chord in use; with nothing patched, chord A is sent
Carries the four notes of the chosen chord as four channels, at a volt per octave
Eight notes set by knob in any temperament from 1 to 34 notes per octave, each on its own output and together on a polyphonic one
Sets that note within the octave, from 0 up to one less than the notes-per-octave setting
Sets the octave of that note, -4 to +4
Carries that note's pitch on its own, at a volt per octave
Sets the temperament, 1 to 34 notes in the octave, starting at 12
Sets how many of the eight notes the polyphonic output carries, 1 to 8; a blue lamp marks each note being sent
Carries the notes within the channel count as one polyphonic signal, at a volt per octave
Sets one note in any temperament from 1 to 34 notes per octave, and breaks an incoming pitch into an octave number and a note number for a pair of voltmeters
Sets the octave of the pitch output, -5 to +5
Sets the note within the octave of the pitch output, from 0 up to one less than the notes-per-octave setting
Carries the pitch set by the octave and note knobs, at a volt per octave, on one channel
The pitch to be broken into an octave number and a note number, polyphonic; with nothing patched here the module reads its own V/Oct output instead
Rounds the note output to whole numbers, so a voltmeter reads 3 rather than 2.999; it is off at power-up and switches off whenever the temperament is changed
The octave number of the incoming pitch, as that many volts, polyphonic
The note number within the octave of the incoming pitch, as that many volts, polyphonic
Sets the temperament, 1 to 34 notes in the octave, starting at 12
Captures the highest and lowest voltage each channel of two signals has reached, for tracking down pops and clicks
The signal whose peaks are captured, polyphonic
The highest voltage that signal has reached on each channel since its last reset
The lowest voltage that signal has reached on each channel since its last reset
Clears the captured peaks for that signal and starts the capture again
Sets the voltage at which the red lamps come on, 0-12V, starting at 12V; a lamp lights when any channel goes above it or below its negative
Note — the captured peaks show in the tooltip of each output port whether or not anything is patched to it
Gathers four polyphonic signals into one, and splits a polyphonic signal back into four of the same channel widths, in two sections that are not connected to each other
One of the polyphonic signals gathered into the merge output; the inputs are taken in order, and one left unpatched adds no channels
Carries the channels of the four merge inputs one after another, clamped to 16 channels with a red lamp on when there would be more
The polyphonic signal split back out, usually the return from whatever processed the merge output
Carries the channels that came from the merge input of the same number; a blue lamp means the counts match, a red one that the output has too many or too few
Note — the resplit outputs give back the original channel widths only while the resplit input carries the signal that came from the merge output
Note — a merge input left empty adds no channels to the merge output, so the resplit output of that same number has to be skipped as well
Shares the channels of one polyphonic signal out over up to four polyphonic outputs, with the split points chosen by button
Makes that channel number a split point, so the channels under it leave on one output and the channels from it upward on the next; it dims while it is being ignored
The polyphonic signal whose channels are shared out, its channel count shown on the blue lamps
Carries one run of channels from the input, between one split point and the next; with no split points chosen at all, every channel goes to the first output
Sixteen buttons putting out 0V or 10V, one polyphonic channel each, on a single cable
Toggles that channel of the output between 0V and 10V
Sets how many channel buttons are in use, which takes a press of one second; the buttons past that point are dimmed and left out of the output, and switching it off again puts all sixteen back
Carries the channel buttons in use, 0V for a button off and 10V for one on
Menu — Radio Buttons — makes the channel buttons exclusive, so pressing one clears the others; with it off, the default, each button toggles on its own
Twelve-note quantizer, snapping a pitch to the notes chosen on its buttons
Puts that note of the octave into the scale or takes it out; the root is the bottom button, and with no note chosen only the root is used
Sets the scale from twelve polyphonic channels, 0V for a note left out and 10V for one in; the note buttons then show the scale arriving here
Sets the root note of the scale at a volt per octave, quantized to the nearest semitone, polyphonic
Chooses whether a pitch between scale notes moves down, to the nearest note either way, or up
Equi-likely quantizing makes every note of the scale equally likely from a random input, rather than wide intervals catching more of the range
The pitch to be quantized, at a volt per octave, polyphonic
The quantized pitch, at a volt per octave, polyphonic
A 10V pulse lasting 1ms each time the quantized note changes, one channel per input channel
Menu — Preset — lists fourteen scales under Factory presets: chromatic, the seven modes of the major scale, harmonic and melodic minor, major and minor pentatonic, blues and whole tone
Quantizer for any temperament from 1 to 34 notes per octave, where the notes allowed are chosen as tuning intervals rather than by number
Chooses that interval, written as a frequency ratio, as one the quantizer should allow; a note of the temperament becomes valid when it falls within the tolerance of a chosen interval
Shows how closely that interval matches a valid note, the brighter half pointing towards the note: top for sharper, bottom for flatter, both halves full for a match within 2.5 cents
Marks that numbered note of the temperament as one the quantizer will use
Lights every interval lying within the tolerance of a valid note
Turns off every interval except the unison
Lights the small-number intervals lying within the tolerance of a valid note
Turns off every interval that has no lamp showing
Sets how close an interval must be to a note of the temperament for that note to count as valid, 0 to 50 cents, starting at 20 cents
Sets the temperament, 1 to 34 notes in the octave, starting at 12
Chooses whether a pitch between valid notes moves down, to the nearest note either way, or up
Equi-likely quantizing makes every valid note equally likely from a random input, rather than wide intervals catching more of the range
The pitch to be quantized, at a volt per octave, polyphonic
The quantized pitch, at a volt per octave, polyphonic
Sets the root note of the scale at a volt per octave, quantized, polyphonic
A 10V pulse lasting 1ms each time the quantized note changes, one channel per input channel
Note — pressing any interval lamp or note lamp highlights the note it belongs to and every interval that matches that note
Quantizer for any temperament from 1 to 34 notes per octave, with the notes it will use picked out by number
Puts that numbered note of the temperament into the scale or takes it out; note 0 is the root, and notes beyond the temperament's count are dimmed and ignored
Turns on every note up to one less than the notes-per-octave setting
Turns off every note except the root
Rotates the scale to its next mode, so a major scale steps through Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian and the rest and comes back after seven presses
A short press shows or hides the blue reference lamps; a press of 2 seconds or more sets those lamps from the notes chosen now
Sets the temperament, 1 to 34 notes in the octave, starting at 12
Sets the root note of the scale at a volt per octave, quantized, polyphonic
Chooses whether a pitch between scale notes moves down, to the nearest note either way, or up
Equi-likely quantizing makes every note of the scale equally likely from a random input, rather than wide intervals catching more of the range
The pitch to be quantized, at a volt per octave, polyphonic
The quantized pitch, at a volt per octave, polyphonic
A 10V pulse lasting 1ms each time the quantized note changes, one channel per input channel
Note — the blue reference lamps are only a visual guide to a scale, and they keep their setting when the patch is closed and opened again
Three chains that delay a polyphonic signal by whole samples, for lining one signal path up with another
The signal that chain delays, polyphonic
That chain's input delayed by one sample
That chain's input delayed by two samples
Note — a chain whose input is unpatched carries on from the chain above it, so leaving the second and third inputs empty gives up to six samples of delay from the first input
Sends a twelve-note scale to the Scale input of the Quant quantizer, as twelve polyphonic channels
Puts that note of the octave into the scale or takes it out; the root is the bottom button
Carries the twelve note buttons as twelve polyphonic channels, 0V for a note left out and 10V for one in
Note — this makes no sound and changes no pitch on its own; patch its output to the Scale input of a Quant, where the twelve channels take over that quantizer's note buttons
Menu — Preset — lists fourteen scales under Factory presets: chromatic, the seven modes of the major scale, harmonic and melodic minor, major and minor pentatonic, blues and whole tone
Splits the first eight channels of a polyphonic cable into eight separate signals
The polyphonic signal whose channels are sent out separately
Carries the channel of that number from the polyphonic input, on its own
Spreads one line of notes across polyphonic channels in turn, so each note's release can keep sounding while the next note starts, and adds a polyphonic amplifier
The signal the amplifier works on, polyphonic
The amplifier's output
Controls the amplifier's level, 0-10V, polyphonic
Sets the amplifier's overall gain, from silence to unity
One line of note pitches at a volt per octave, each pitch held when its gate arrives
The note pitches spread over the channels in turn, at a volt per octave, for a polyphonic oscillator
One line of gates, one per note; each new gate moves the next note to the next channel
Each note's gate on its own channel, keeping the length it arrived with
Sets how many channels the notes are spread over, 1 to 5, starting at 2
Note — only one note sounds at a time, so chords do not pass through; a polyphonic oscillator and a polyphonic envelope generator are both needed for the tails to be heard
Menu — Latch mode — sets when the pitch is taken: Gate rise as the gate opens, Gate fall as the gate closes, Next note not until the following gate; each mode sets its own five-sample offset
Four blocks that each spread one line of notes across polyphonic channels in turn, merged onto one pair of outputs, with a polyphonic amplifier and a resplit section
One line of note pitches at a volt per octave for one of the four blocks; with the pitch poly-merge button on, the channels arriving here are handed to the blocks instead
One line of gates for one of the four blocks; with the gate poly-merge button on, the channels arriving here are handed to the blocks instead
Switches the four pitch inputs to polyphonic, so their channels are given to the blocks in order from the first input, ignoring gaps; a blue lamp shows it is on
Switches the four gate inputs to polyphonic, so their channels are given to the blocks in order from the first input, ignoring gaps; a blue lamp shows it is on
Every block's note pitches on one polyphonic cable, at a volt per octave, for a polyphonic oscillator
Every block's gates on one polyphonic cable, for a polyphonic oscillator or envelope generator
Sets how many channels each block spreads its notes over, 1 to 5, starting at 2; a red lamp comes on when the total would pass 16 channels and the count is cut back
The polyphonic return from whatever the pitch and gate outputs are driving, to be split back into blocks
Carries one block's worth of channels from the resplit input, as many channels as the channel knob is set to
The signal the amplifier works on, polyphonic
The amplifier's output
Controls the amplifier's level, 0-10V, polyphonic
Sets the amplifier's overall gain, from silence to unity
Note — with the inputs monophonic, a pitch or gate patched to one input is passed back to the lower-numbered inputs as well, and the blue lamps beside the inputs show which blocks are being fed
Note — a block runs only when it is being fed both a pitch and a gate, so the blue lamp beside a pitch input and the blue lamp beside the gate input of the same number both have to be on
Menu — Latch mode — sets when a block takes its pitch: Gate rise as the gate opens, Gate fall as the gate closes, Next note not until the following gate; each mode sets its own five-sample offset
Four buffers that each delay a polyphonic signal by a chosen number of whole samples
The signal that buffer delays, polyphonic
That buffer's input, delayed by the number of samples set on its knob
Sets the delay for that buffer, 1 to 9 samples, starting at 5
Note — the four buffers are separate from one another, so patch one output into the next input for more than nine samples of delay
Three separate polyphonic amplifiers, each with a control input and a gain knob
The signal that amplifier works on, polyphonic
That amplifier's output
Controls that amplifier's level, 0-10V, polyphonic
Sets that amplifier's overall gain, from silence to unity
Note — an amplifier whose CV input is unpatched passes its input at the level set by its gain knob, and a CV with fewer channels than the signal holds its last channel across the rest
Four separate polyphonic amplifiers, each with a gain knob
The signal that amplifier works on, polyphonic
That amplifier's output
Sets that amplifier's gain, from silence to unity
